measured: 2026-10-16, Chrome, fonts loaded, ?fill=1, v3 palette, header/rail/footer inset to the cards, deputy quote on Aug. 24, agents photo on Sept. 3
note: The deck and the source line set the height at the narrowest columns. Both are inset to the cards, so they wrap sooner than before 16 Oct.
formula: three segments chosen by gates: s1 = 1767px - 1.829*COL below a 413px column, s2 = 1317px - 0.637*COL to 577px, s3 = 1494px - 0.922*COL above
fit: never short at any measured width; spare averages 44px, peaks at 77px
why_no_step: A single sloped clamp covers both layouts, so there is no step in the formula and therefore none of the 17px Windows-scrollbar band that a stepped formula creates at a breakpoint.
watch_the_source_line: The footer source line sets the height at the narrowest columns: adding '(MPI)' made it wrap to an extra line below a 360px column and added 17px there. Re-measure after any edit to it.
card_width: The stage bleeds --peek past the column on each side so the card stays the full column width; .tl has overflow-x: clip so that overhang cannot widen the page. Without the clip it added a horizontal scrollbar inside the article iframe.
why_the_gate: A single sloped clamp over both layouts wasted up to 141px. The gate switches regimes at a 577px column instead of the 560px breakpoint, because on Windows with classic scrollbars 100vw reads about 17px wider than the real column.
scrollbar_guard: 17px above a 560px column, 6px below it. The style runs in the host page where Windows classic scrollbars inflate 100vw by ~17px; applying the full 17px at phone widths cost about 100px of height for a case that does not occur.
